A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optical properties of diffused waveguiding structures in LiNbO3 are determined by the parameters of the titanium diffusion process, which are in turn determined by the technological conditions.

the results of the present study have made it possible to obtain an adequate mathematical description of the titanium diffusion into LiNB03, and to determine the parameters of the waveguides fabricated by different methods.

we have developed an experimental method and a mathematical model that can be used to fabricate optical waveguides with a desired transverse refractive-index distribution and to determine their characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the refractive index profile can be calculated with a high degree of accuracy by using the diffusion model.

the refractive index distribution is not a Gaussian function, as is usually assumed, but rather is a function of the form exp[-(z/2a)(1 + (z/b)2)], where a and b are the parameters that characterize the waveguide.

it is possible to obtain waveguides with a refractive index distribution close to the optimum one, which is characterized by the absence of a maximum in the refractive index distribution, by using a mathematical model of the diffusion process.
